newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares close below highs, hit by weaker BTPs.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares close below highs, hit by weaker BTPs.

text.p: Italian shares closed firmer but below the day's highs, as a downturn in BTP futures took the edge of the market in which turnover was boosted by the expiry of options contracts and heavy trading in selected stocks.

The all-share Mibtel index finished 0.77 percent higher at 12,500 while the blue chip Mib30 index advanced 0.86 percent to 18,708. Turnover totalled 1.978 trillion lire ($1.2 billion) with some 450 billion lire linked to options expiry.
Credito Italiano saw its shares come down 3.91 percent to 2,580 lire at the close on profit-taking and a wave of arbitrage activity involving warrants on the stock.
Some investors were buying Credito warrants, exercisable on November 30 1997 at 1,750 lire and were selling the underlying shares thereby pushing down their price, brokers said.

Fiat shares were hit by concerns over reported Brazilian government plans to impose tax changes affecting hire purchases of cars. The group's stock closed 1.02 percent lower at 5,520 lire. Fiat is a major car producer in Brazil.
Energy concern ENI advanced 1.9 percent to close at 9.079 lire, boosted by increased estimates of the reserves of an Angolan oilfield in which the company owns a stake.
Shares in TIM closed 0.73 percent lower at 5,137 lire, on profit-taking after the company reported a 29 percent rise in first quarter sales to around two trillion lire.
